title: Jaw Pain at a Therapy Practice: R vs Z vs F Codes

cards.title: Case: A Client Asks a Therapist About Jaw Pain
cards.content:
A client calls a mental health practice and asks to be seen by a therapist for **jaw pain**. The front desk asks billing two questions: *Is that normal?* and *Can we bill it with an R code or a Z code?*

This case walks through:
• who treats jaw pain and who treats the psychological side of it
• why the jaw-pain symptom code is not the diagnosis for a therapy claim
• the mental health codes that can fit, and the official rules for each
• what the coder should do before the claim goes out

Every code and rule here was checked against the **FY 2027 ICD-10-CM code set and Tabular List (CMS)** and the **FY 2027 Official Guidelines**.

cards.title: Who Treats What
cards.content:
**Jaw pain itself is a physical symptom.** A medical or dental provider evaluates it, for example for a temporomandibular joint (TMJ) problem or teeth grinding.

**A therapist** (LMFT, LCSW, psychologist) diagnoses and treats mental, emotional and behavioral conditions. Therapy is appropriate when there is a psychological side to the pain, such as:
• stress or anxiety that leads to clenching or grinding
• coping with ongoing pain

In that case the therapist treats the mental health piece, ideally while the client's medical or dental provider handles the jaw.

*This is general scope-of-practice information, not a legal ruling. Check the licensing board's rules for the specific license.*

cards.title: Why R68.84 Is Not the Therapy Diagnosis
cards.content:
**R68.84, Jaw pain** is a real code (Chapter 18, symptoms and signs). The Tabular List gives these inclusion terms: *Mandibular pain*, *Maxilla pain*. It has an **Excludes1** note: *temporomandibular joint arthralgia (M26.62-)*.

It is a **medical symptom code**. A therapist does not diagnose or treat jaw pain, so R68.84 is not the diagnosis that supports a psychotherapy claim. The claim needs the **mental health diagnosis the therapist documents** after the assessment.

*I cannot confirm how each payer handles R-code-only psychotherapy claims; check the payer's behavioral health policy.*

TMJ arthralgia (M26.62-) is coded there instead.

cards.title: Why There Is No Z Code for This
cards.content:
Z codes (Chapter 21) describe **reasons for an encounter or a status**, such as screening, counseling, aftercare or a history of a condition. None of them describes jaw pain.

For example, **Z13.31, Encounter for screening for depression** is for screening a person **without symptoms**. A client who reports a problem is not being screened: the official guidelines (Section I.C.21.c.5) say testing because of a sign or symptom is a diagnostic examination, not a screening.

cards.question: A therapist sees a client who asks for help with jaw pain. Which code is a medical symptom code that should NOT be used as the diagnosis for the psychotherapy claim?
options: F45.42, Pain disorder with related psychological factors
F54, Psychological and behavioral factors associated with disorders or diseases classified elsewhere
cards.explanation: R68.84 is a Chapter 18 symptom code for jaw pain, which a medical or dental provider evaluates; a therapist does not diagnose or treat the jaw. F45.42, F45.8 and F54 are Chapter 5 mental and behavioral codes that can describe the psychological side, if the therapist documents that diagnosis.

visual.hint: Which code is about the jaw itself?

cards.title: Option 1: F45.42, Pain Disorder With Related Psychological Factors
cards.content:
**F45.42, Pain disorder with related psychological factors** fits when the pain has a physical cause **and** psychological factors play a part.

The official guideline (Section I.C.5.a) says: *"Code F45.42, Pain disorders with related psychological factors, should be used with a code from category G89, Pain, not elsewhere classified, if there is documentation of a psychological component for a patient with acute or chronic pain."*

The Tabular List matches it: under F45.42, **Code also** associated acute or chronic pain (G89.-).

So F45.42 is reported **together with a G89 pain code**, when the documentation supports both.

boxes.b: Code also acute or chronic pain (G89.-).

cards.title: Option 2: F45.41, Pain Exclusively Psychological
cards.content:
**F45.41, Pain disorder exclusively related to psychological factors** is for pain that is **entirely** psychological. Its Tabular inclusion term is *Somatoform pain disorder (persistent)*.

Section I.C.5.a: *"Assign code F45.41, for pain that is exclusively related to psychological disorders. As indicated by the Excludes 1 note under category G89, a code from category G89 should not be assigned with code F45.41."*

**Exam trap:** F45.42 goes **with** a G89 code; F45.41 goes **without** one.

boxes.b: Psychological factors. Add a G89 code.

cards.title: Option 3: F45.8 for Psychogenic Teeth Grinding
cards.content:
If stress-related clenching or grinding is the issue, look at **F45.8, Other somatoform disorders**. Its Tabular inclusion terms include **"Teeth grinding"**.

F45.8 has an **Excludes1** note: *sleep related teeth grinding (G47.63)*. And **G47.63, Sleep related bruxism** has the matching Excludes1: *psychogenic bruxism (F45.8)*.

So the two never go together:
• **Psychogenic** (stress-driven) grinding → F45.8
• **Sleep-related** grinding → G47.63, a sleep disorder that a medical provider diagnoses

visual.title: TEETH GRINDING
visual.sub: Two codes that exclude each other

cards.title: Option 4: F54, Psychological Factors Affecting a Physical Condition
cards.content:
**F54, Psychological and behavioral factors associated with disorders or diseases classified elsewhere** has the inclusion term *Psychological factors affecting physical conditions*.

The Tabular List says **Code first** the associated physical disorder. Its examples are asthma, dermatitis, gastric ulcer, mucous colitis, ulcerative colitis and urticaria.

That means F54 is never reported alone: a **physical diagnosis must be documented** (by the provider who diagnosed it) and sequenced **first**.

F54 has an **Excludes2** note for *tension-type headache (G44.2)*.

visual.title: F54
visual.sub: Psychological factors affecting a physical condition

cards.title: Option 5: The Therapist's Own Diagnosis
cards.content:
Often the cleanest code is simply **the mental health condition the therapist diagnoses**, for example an anxiety, stress-related or adjustment disorder, when stress is what drives the clenching.

The coder does not choose the diagnosis. **The code must match what the therapist documents** after the assessment. If the record only says "client wants help with jaw pain," there is nothing to code yet: query the therapist for the diagnosis.

cards.question: A therapist documents that a client's chronic jaw pain has a psychological component. Per Section I.C.5.a, how is F45.42 reported?
options: With a code from category G89, Pain, not elsewhere classified
With R68.84 as the first-listed code
cards.explanation: Section I.C.5.a says F45.42 "should be used with a code from category G89 ... if there is documentation of a psychological component for a patient with acute or chronic pain," and the Tabular List says code also G89.-. Reporting it alone ignores that instruction. R68.84 is a medical symptom code, not part of this rule. Z13 codes are for screening people without symptoms.

visual.hint: Section I.C.5.a names the category to pair it with.

cards.question: A therapist documents stress-driven daytime teeth grinding (psychogenic). Which code fits, and which code must NOT be added with it?
cards.explanation: F45.8 includes "Teeth grinding" and has an Excludes1 note for sleep related teeth grinding (G47.63); G47.63 in turn excludes psychogenic bruxism (F45.8). So psychogenic grinding is F45.8 and the two are never reported together. G47.63 is the sleep-related (medical) type. F54 cannot be reported alone because it needs a physical disorder coded first. R68.84 is a jaw-pain symptom code.

cards.question: A coder wants to report F54 for a therapy client. What does the Tabular List require first?
options: The associated physical disorder, coded first
cards.explanation: F54 carries a "Code first the associated physical disorder" note, so a documented physical diagnosis must be sequenced before it. The G89 pairing rule belongs to F45.42, not F54. Z13 codes are screening codes. F54 cannot stand alone because of the code-first note.

cards.title: What the Coder Does With This Request
cards.content:
1. **Scheduling:** it is appropriate to book a therapy assessment if the client wants help with the stress, anxiety or coping side of the jaw pain. Suggest the client also see their medical or dental provider about the jaw itself.
2. **After the visit:** read the therapist's documentation. Do not code from the reason for the call.
3. **Match the diagnosis:** pick the code that matches what the therapist documented (F45.42 + G89, F45.41, F45.8, F54 + the physical disorder first, or the therapist's anxiety/stress diagnosis).
4. **Check the code notes:** G89 with F45.42 but never with F45.41; F45.8 never with G47.63; F54 always after the physical disorder.
5. **Query** if the documentation does not state a mental health diagnosis.
6. **Check the payer's behavioral health policy** before submitting.

cards.title: What We Could Not Confirm
cards.content:
These points were **not** verified and should be checked before relying on them:

• **Payer acceptance:** whether Partnership HealthPlan, Medi-Cal or commercial payers accept F45.42, F45.8 or F54 with psychotherapy CPT codes (90832/90834/90837), or deny claims with only an R code. Check each payer's behavioral health policy.
• **Health behavior codes:** some payers cover a separate group of CPT codes for psychological factors affecting a physical condition (health behavior assessment and intervention). Those CPT codes and their coverage were not verified here.
• **Scope of practice:** the split between medical/dental and therapy care is general information; confirm specifics with the licensing board.

cards.title: Key Takeaways
cards.content:
• Therapy for jaw pain is normal **for the psychological side** (stress, clenching, coping), not for the jaw itself.
• **R68.84, Jaw pain** is a medical symptom code, not the therapist's diagnosis.
• **No Z code** describes jaw pain; Z13.31 is depression screening for people without symptoms.
• **F45.42** + a **G89** code when pain has a psychological component (Section I.C.5.a).
• **F45.41** for exclusively psychological pain, **never with G89**.
• **F45.8** includes psychogenic teeth grinding; it excludes **G47.63** (sleep related bruxism).
• **F54** needs the **physical disorder coded first**.
• Code only what the therapist documents; query when it is unclear.

*Sources: CMS FY 2027 ICD-10-CM code descriptions and Tabular List; ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY 2027, Section I.C.5.a.*
